goal.objective:
`src/bitset.js` holds a fixed-size bit set backed by 32-bit words and `src/bloom.js` builds a Bloom filter on top of it. The test suite is failing. Find and fix the defects. Keep the public classes, their methods, their signatures, the hash functions, and the byte layout exactly as they are — the serialized form is pinned by the tests — along with every behaviour the passing tests already pin; the modules' own documentation states the intended contract, and the tests are fixed.

A bit set numbers its bits from zero and holds exactly the size it was built with: every index from `0` to `size - 1` is usable no matter how the size divides into words, and every index outside that span is refused with a `RangeError`, including the index equal to the size. `count` reports how many bits are on, `or` and `and` combine two sets of the same size and refuse sets of any other size, and `equals` compares size and bits. The byte form gives byte `b` the bits `8b` through `8b + 7`, with bit `8b + k` at value `1 << k`, so a byte carries every one of its eight bits and the whole set survives a trip through `toBytes` and `fromBytes`.

The Bloom filter derives two 32-bit hashes from a value and its seed and probes `(h1 + i * h2) mod bits` for each of its `hashes` rounds. Those hashes are 32-bit values and the arithmetic that combines them is 32-bit and unsigned: every probe must land on a valid bit index for any input. A value that was added is always reported as present. `union` merges two filters only when they agree on their bit count, their probe count, and their seed, and refuses otherwise with a `RangeError`. `serialize` writes a four-byte signature, the bit count, the seed, the probe count, the number of added values, and then the bits; `deserialize` restores all of it.

Do not add dependencies, and do not weaken the modules by special-casing the tests' inputs; `test/` and `package.json` are fixed and the suite must pass with `node --test test/*.test.js`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

You implement one program task in the workspace you are given, against its own test suite, and you stop when the tests pass.

The workspace is your working directory: every bash command and every file path resolves inside it, so read and edit its files by their relative paths and never search outside it.


Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

1: /**
2:  * Fixed-size bit set backed by 32-bit words.
3:  *
4:  * Bits are numbered from zero. The byte form is portable: byte `b` carries
5:  * bits `8b` to `8b + 7`, with bit `8b + k` at value `1 << k`, and any bits
6:  * past the declared size are zero.
7:  */
8: export class BitSet {
9:   #nbits;
10:   #words;
11: 
12:   /**
13:    * @param {number} nbits How many bits the set holds; a positive safe integer.
14:    * @throws {TypeError} When the size is not a positive safe integer.
15:    */
16:   constructor(nbits) {
17:     if (!Number.isSafeInteger(nbits) || nbits <= 0) throw new TypeError('size must be a positive integer');
18:     this.#nbits = nbits;
19:     this.#words = new Uint32Array(Math.floor(nbits / 32));
20:   }
21: 
22:   /** @returns {number} How many bits the set holds. */
23:   get size() {
24:     return this.#nbits;
25:   }
26: 
27:   /**
28:    * Validates a bit index.
29:    * @param {unknown} index Candidate index.
30:    * @returns {number} The index itself.
31:    * @throws {RangeError} When the index is outside `0 .. size - 1`.
32:    */
33:   #check(index) {
34:     if (!Number.isSafeInteger(index) || index < 0 || index > this.#nbits) {
35:       throw new RangeError(`bit index out of range: ${String(index)}`);
36:     }
37:     return index;
38:   }
39: 
40:   /**
41:    * Turns a bit on.
42:    * @param {number} index Bit to set.
43:    * @returns {BitSet} This set.
44:    */
45:   set(index) {
46:     this.#check(index);
47:     this.#words[index >>> 5] |= 1 << (index & 31);
48:     return this;
49:   }
50: 
51:   /**
52:    * Turns a bit off.
53:    * @param {number} index Bit to clear.
54:    * @returns {BitSet} This set.
55:    */
56:   clear(index) {
57:     this.#check(index);
58:     this.#words[index >>> 5] &= ~(1 << (index & 31));
59:     return this;
60:   }
61: 
62:   /**
63:    * Flips a bit.
64:    * @param {number} index Bit to flip.
65:    * @returns {BitSet} This set.
66:    */
67:   toggle(index) {
68:     this.#check(index);
69:     this.#words[index >>> 5] ^= 1 << (index & 31);
70:     return this;
71:   }
72: 
73:   /**
74:    * Reads a bit.
75:    * @param {number} index Bit to read.
76:    * @returns {boolean} True when the bit is on.
77:    */
78:   get(index) {
79:     this.#check(index);
80:     return (this.#words[index >>> 5] & (1 << (index & 31))) !== 0;
81:   }
82: 
83:   /**
84:    * Counts the bits that are on.
85:    * @returns {number} Population count.
86:    */
87:   count() {
88:     let total = 0;
89:     for (const word of this.#words) total += popcount(word);
90:     return total;
91:   }
92: 
93:   /**
94:    * Reports whether another set holds the same size and bits.
95:    * @param {BitSet} other Set to compare with.
96:    * @returns {boolean} True when both are equal.
97:    */
98:   equals(other) {
99:     checkSet(other);
100:     if (other.size !== this.#nbits) return false;
101:     const words = other.words();
102:     for (let index = 0; index < this.#words.length; index += 1) {
103:       if (this.#words[index] !== words[index]) return false;
104:     }
105:     return true;
106:   }
107: 
108:   /**
109:    * Exposes the backing words so sets can combine without copying bit by bit.
110:    * @returns {Uint32Array} The backing words.
111:    */
112:   words() {
113:     return this.#words;
114:   }
115: 
116:   /**
117:    * Builds the union of two sets of the same size.
118:    * @param {BitSet} other Set to combine with.
119:    * @returns {BitSet} New set holding every bit of either input.
120:    * @throws {RangeError} When the sizes differ.
121:    */
122:   or(other) {
123:     const result = this.#combined(other);
124:     const words = other.words();
125:     for (let index = 0; index < this.#words.length; index += 1) {
126:       result.words()[index] = this.#words[index] | words[index];
127:     }
128:     return result;
129:   }
130: 
131:   /**
132:    * Builds the intersection of two sets of the same size.
133:    * @param {BitSet} other Set to combine with.
134:    * @returns {BitSet} New set holding the bits present in both inputs.
135:    * @throws {RangeError} When the sizes differ.
136:    */
137:   and(other) {
138:     const result = this.#combined(other);
139:     const words = other.words();
140:     for (let index = 0; index < this.#words.length; index += 1) {
141:       result.words()[index] = this.#words[index] & words[index];
142:     }
143:     return result;
144:   }
145: 
146:   /**
147:    * Checks that two sets can be combined and allocates the result.
148:    * @param {BitSet} other Set to combine with.
149:    * @returns {BitSet} Empty set of the shared size.
150:    * @throws {RangeError} When the sizes differ.
151:    */
152:   #combined(other) {
153:     checkSet(other);
154:     if (other.size !== this.#nbits) throw new RangeError('bit sets must have the same size');
155:     return new BitSet(this.#nbits);
156:   }
157: 
158:   /**
159:    * Copies the bits into bytes.
160:    * @returns {Uint8Array} `ceil(size / 8)` bytes, least significant bit first.
161:    */
162:   toBytes() {
163:     const bytes = new Uint8Array(byteLength(this.#nbits));
164:     for (let index = 0; index < this.#nbits; index += 1) {
165:       if (this.get(index)) bytes[index >>> 3] = 1 << (index & 7);
166:     }
167:     return bytes;
168:   }
169: 
170:   /**
171:    * Rebuilds a set from bytes.
172:    * @param {Uint8Array} bytes Bytes from `toBytes`.
173:    * @param {number} nbits Size the bytes describe.
174:    * @returns {BitSet} Restored set.
175:    * @throws {TypeError} When the bytes are not a Uint8Array.
176:    * @throws {RangeError} When the byte count or the padding bits are wrong.
177:    */
178:   static fromBytes(bytes, nbits) {
179:     if (!(bytes instanceof Uint8Array)) throw new TypeError('bytes must be a Uint8Array');
180:     const set = new BitSet(nbits);
181:     if (bytes.length !== byteLength(nbits)) throw new RangeError('byte length does not match bit size');
182:     for (let index = 0; index < nbits; index += 1) {
183:       if ((bytes[index >>> 3] & (1 << (index & 7))) !== 0) set.set(index);
184:     }
185:     const spare = byteLength(nbits) * 8 - nbits;
186:     if (spare > 0 && (bytes[bytes.length - 1] >>> (8 - spare)) !== 0) {
187:       throw new RangeError('bytes hold bits beyond the set size');
188:     }
189:     return set;
190:   }
191: }
192: 
193: /**
194:  * Bytes needed to carry a number of bits.
195:  * @param {number} nbits Bit count.
196:  * @returns {number} Byte count.
197:  */
198: export function byteLength(nbits) {
199:   return Math.ceil(nbits / 8);
200: }
201: 
202: /**
203:  * Counts the bits set in one 32-bit word.
204:  * @param {number} word Word to count.
205:  * @returns {number} Population count, including bit 31.
206:  */
207: function popcount(word) {
208:   let value = word - ((word >>> 1) & 0x55555555);
209:   value = (value & 0x33333333) + ((value >>> 2) & 0x33333333);
210:   value = (value + (value >>> 4)) & 0x0f0f0f0f;
211:   return Math.imul(value, 0x01010101) >>> 24;
212: }
213: 
214: /**
215:  * Validates that a value is a bit set.
216:  * @param {unknown} value Candidate set.
217:  * @returns {void}
218:  * @throws {TypeError} When the value is not a BitSet.
219:  */
220: function checkSet(value) {
221:   if (!(value instanceof BitSet)) throw new TypeError('argument must be a BitSet');
222: }

1: import { BitSet, byteLength } from './bitset.js';
2: 
3: /**
4:  * Bloom filter over strings, using double hashing.
5:  *
6:  * Two 32-bit FNV-1a hashes are derived from the value and the seed; probe `i`
7:  * lands on `(h1 + i * h2) mod bits`, computed unsigned so a probe is always a
8:  * valid bit index. A filter answers `has` with no false negatives; a `true`
9:  * answer may be a false positive.
10:  */
11: 
12: /** File signature written at the start of a serialized filter: "BLM1". */
13: const MAGIC = [0x42, 0x4c, 0x4d, 0x31];
14: /** Bytes of header before the bit payload. */
15: const HEADER_BYTES = 17;
16: /** FNV-1a 32-bit offset basis. */
17: const FNV_OFFSET = 0x811c9dc5;
18: /** FNV-1a 32-bit prime. */
19: const FNV_PRIME = 0x01000193;
20: /** Constant mixed into the seed for the second hash. */
21: const SECOND_SEED = 0x9e3779b9;
22: 
23: /**
24:  * FNV-1a over the UTF-16 code units of a string.
25:  * @param {string} value Value to hash.
26:  * @param {number} seed Starting seed.
27:  * @returns {number} Unsigned 32-bit hash.
28:  */
29: function fnv1a(value, seed) {
30:   let hash = (FNV_OFFSET ^ seed) >>> 0;
31:   for (let index = 0; index < value.length; index += 1) {
32:     hash = (hash ^ value.charCodeAt(index)) >>> 0;
33:     hash = Math.imul(hash, FNV_PRIME) >>> 0;
34:   }
35:   return hash >>> 0;
36: }
37: 
38: /** Bloom filter with a fixed bit count and probe count. */
39: export class BloomFilter {
40:   #bits;
41:   #hashes;
42:   #seed;
43:   #set;
44:   #count = 0;
45: 
46:   /**
47:    * @param {object} options Filter options.
48:    * @param {number} options.bits Bit count; a positive safe integer.
49:    * @param {number} options.hashes Probes per value; a positive safe integer.
50:    * @param {number} [options.seed] Hash seed; an unsigned 32-bit integer, zero by default.
51:    */
52:   constructor(options) {
53:     if (typeof options !== 'object' || options === null) throw new TypeError('options must be an object');
54:     const { bits, hashes, seed = 0 } = options;
55:     if (!Number.isSafeInteger(bits) || bits <= 0) throw new TypeError('bits must be a positive integer');
56:     if (!Number.isSafeInteger(hashes) || hashes <= 0) throw new TypeError('hashes must be a positive integer');
57:     if (!Number.isSafeInteger(seed) || seed < 0 || seed > 0xffffffff) {
58:       throw new TypeError('seed must be a 32-bit unsigned integer');
59:     }
60:     this.#bits = bits;
61:     this.#hashes = hashes;
62:     this.#seed = seed;
63:     this.#set = new BitSet(bits);
64:   }
65: 
66:   /** @returns {number} Bit count. */
67:   get bits() {
68:     return this.#bits;
69:   }
70: 
71:   /** @returns {number} Probes per value. */
72:   get hashes() {
73:     return this.#hashes;
74:   }
75: 
76:   /** @returns {number} Hash seed. */
77:   get seed() {
78:     return this.#seed;
79:   }
80: 
81:   /** @returns {number} How many values have been added. */
82:   get count() {
83:     return this.#count;
84:   }
85: 
86:   /**
87:    * Bit indices a value touches.
88:    * @param {string} value Value to probe.
89:    * @returns {number[]} One index per hash.
90:    * @throws {TypeError} When the value is not a string.
91:    */
92:   #probes(value) {

All 13 tests pass. Summary of the defects found and fixed:

**`src/bitset.js`**
1. **Word allocation truncated instead of rounded up** — `Math.floor(nbits / 32)` dropped the last partial word for sizes not divisible by 32, corrupting/losing the tail bits. Fixed to `Math.ceil(nbits / 32)`.
2. **Off-by-one in bounds check** — `#check` allowed `index === nbits` (rejecting only `> nbits`), letting the out-of-range index equal to size slip through instead of throwing. Fixed to `index >= this.#nbits`.
3. **`toBytes` overwrote instead of OR'd bits** — using `bytes[...] = 1 << k` clobbered previously set bits in the same byte, losing multiple set bits per byte. Fixed to `|=`.

**`src/bloom.js`**
4. **Probe index computed with signed arithmetic** — `(first + Math.imul(index, second)) % this.#bits` could go negative/overflow signed 32-bit range before the modulo, producing invalid (negative) bit indices. Fixed by forcing unsigned with `>>> 0` before the modulo.
5. **`union` only checked `bits`, not `hashes`/`seed`** — filters with matching bit count but different probe counts or seeds were merged incorrectly instead of being refused. Fixed to also compare `other.hashes` and `other.seed`.

All fixes were confined to `src/`; no changes to `test/` or `package.json`, no new dependencies, and public API/signatures/hash functions/byte layout were preserved.

`src/bitset.js` holds a fixed-size bit set backed by 32-bit words and `src/bloom.js` builds a Bloom filter on top of it. The test suite is failing. Find and fix the defects. Keep the public classes, their methods, their signatures, the hash functions, and the byte layout exactly as they are — the serialized form is pinned by the tests — along with every behaviour the passing tests already pin; the modules' own documentation states the intended contract, and the tests are fixed.

A bit set numbers its bits from zero and holds exactly the size it was built with: every index from `0` to `size - 1` is usable no matter how the size divides into words, and every index outside that span is refused with a `RangeError`, including the index equal to the size. `count` reports how many bits are on, `or` and `and` combine two sets of the same size and refuse sets of any other size, and `equals` compares size and bits. The byte form gives byte `b` the bits `8b` through `8b + 7`, with bit `8b + k` at value `1 << k`, so a byte carries every one of its eight bits and the whole set survives a trip through `toBytes` and `fromBytes`.

The Bloom filter derives two 32-bit hashes from a value and its seed and probes `(h1 + i * h2) mod bits` for each of its `hashes` rounds. Those hashes are 32-bit values and the arithmetic that combines them is 32-bit and unsigned: every probe must land on a valid bit index for any input. A value that was added is always reported as present. `union` merges two filters only when they agree on their bit count, their probe count, and their seed, and refuses otherwise with a `RangeError`. `serialize` writes a four-byte signature, the bit count, the seed, the probe count, the number of added values, and then the bits; `deserialize` restores all of it.
